key_insight: A walking surface-code stability circuit suppresses temporally correlated leakage errors, reaching a logical error probability floor of ≤3.20×10⁻⁸ at 60 cycles.
engineering_relevance: Controlling higher-state leakage and adapting syndrome-extraction duration could reduce logical errors and time overhead in fault-tolerant quantum processors.
method: Scale stability experiments from 3×3 to 7×7 patches on a 105-qubit Willow processor.
Model data-qubit heating into |3⟩ and higher-state transport with a parameter-free device-level leakage model.
Implement walking stability circuits and evaluate decoder-confidence-based stopping offline.
evidence_signal: Experiments achieved timelike suppression μ_T=1.47±0.25 and a walking-circuit error floor two orders of magnitude below the standard circuit; offline adaptive stopping reduced spacetime logical error by 38% and time overhead by 34%.
watch_item: Ionizing-radiation error bursts limited the walking circuit, and adaptive stopping was evaluated offline rather than demonstrated in real-time control.
paper_title: Resolving and Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction
